purpose: Define explicit transaction boundaries for multi-write operations so all-or-nothing requirements, ordering and rollback behavior are declared rather than storage-engine assumptions.

topics.name: DWH Transaction and Atomicity
topics.purpose: Define explicit transaction boundaries for multi-write operations so all-or-nothing requirements, ordering and rollback behavior are declared rather than storage-engine assumptions.

semantics.transaction_rule: A multi-write operation declares whether it requires atomic transaction semantics.
semantics.identity_rule: Each transaction has a distinct runtime transaction identity.
semantics.members_rule: Transaction member writes reference exact write execution/target identities.
semantics.atomic_rule: For atomic transactions, either the accepted mutation set commits as one unit or no member becomes accepted state.
semantics.ordering_rule: Member ordering/dependencies are explicit where semantically relevant.
semantics.rollback_rule: Rollback restores pre-transaction accepted state according to the transaction profile and does not erase execution/audit evidence.
semantics.external_rule: Effects outside the transactional store are not claimed atomic unless an explicit distributed/compensation contract supports them.
semantics.failure_rule: Partial commit in an atomic profile is a hard failure requiring explicit recovery state.

invariants.rule: Every DWH mutation resolves an exact destination instance/schema/record/field identity, validates intended change, evaluates authorization and conflict state, and records provenance; no write is inferred from query/display context or silently overwrites conflicting accepted state.

hard_gates.condition: external side effect claimed atomic without contract
member order inferred from filesystem/serialization order
transaction identity conflated with individual write
